N1 lessons, second half: 24 new grammar lessons in eight units (261 lessons in all; N1 has 48): Purpose, dependence and defiance; Occasions, pretexts and turning points; Surprise, emphasis and giving up; Concession and half-commitment; Relations, lists and word-building; Limits, missed chances and restraint; Old forms that are still alive; Formal Japanese at work (top-level keigo, the written style of case reports, speeches and formal greetings). Each form is marked say or understand, with the plain form to say instead.

N1 kanji complete: the other 576 N1 kanji (2,225 kanji in all) on the N1 chart, each with its page, readings, example words, stroke-order diagram and writing sheet. Many of them are met mainly in names, and their pages say so.
Dictionary: 1,202 words from the new kanji pages (about 7,250 in all).

N1 reading and speaking: eight N1 reading passages (40 in all: a sample case report, a sample consent form, a patient-safety newsletter, a patient's notes on getting better, an editorial, a ceremony speech, a literary essay, an essay after one year of training) and six N1 dialogues (28 in all: conference questions, a family's complaint, an older patient who speaks formally, a discharge-support meeting, reporting a near miss, a farewell speech), with 42 listening questions.
Example sentences for 788 N1 words (about 4,070 in all), eight N1 topic-matching sets (60), and 44 N1 verbs and 15 N1 adjectives in the trainer (572 and 322).

N1 in the drills: Fill the blank (192 N1 questions, four for every N1 lesson), Transform the sentence (40), Find the mistake (40), Word pairs (60) and Listen and reply (30). The Level review test now has every section at N1.
The N1 stroke-order data is in two files so that each stays a reasonable size; both are saved for offline use.
